## Natural history notes

A small skeletonizing leaf beetle characterized by a compact oval body, yellowish to brown coloration, and darker markings on the wing covers. In Florida, Neolochmaea dilatipennis is an introduced Neotropical leaf beetle first reported established near Miami, and it is associated with warm open or shrubby habitats where its host plants occur. Adults and larvae feed on leaves, including false buttonweed and related coastal or wetland plants, skeletonizing foliage and serving as prey for spiders, predatory bugs, birds, and parasitoid wasps.
